source.section: Schedule SB (PDF page 1) and its Instructions: line 16 and its Caution (SB Instructions PDF page 7; Publication 126 PDF page 8 section 4.E(1); Publication 106 PDF page 4 section 3.C(1)); line 17 and the Retirement Income Subtraction Worksheet lines 1-6 (SB Instructions PDF page 8; Publication 126 PDF pages 8-9 section 4.E(2)); Form 1 lines 1-12 (Form 1 PDF page 1); Form 1 Instructions PDF page 15 line 8 and lines 10a-10b (PDF pages 15-16), PDF pages 35-37 2025 Standard Deduction Table (row named in worked), PDF page 15 line 12 with the PDF pages 38-43 Tax Table and PDF page 44 Tax Computation Worksheet; tax figured from the 2025 Tax Rate Schedules, Publication 106 PDF pages 6-7

worked: Married filing jointly, you 68, spouse 65: you IRA 200, spouse IRA 1,000, interest 28,700; federal AGI 29,900 under 30,000. The form stacks the two subtractions across the spouses: line 16 takes your 200 (you are 67; the spouse is not); line 17 worksheet column A line 3 200, line 4 200 (your line 16), line 5 0, line 6 0; column B line 5 1,000, line 6 1,000; line 17 1,000. The projection applies line 17 to the full qualifying income, so it also gives you the smaller of 200 and 5,000 = 200: line 17 1,200; expected follows the projection (accepted approximation). Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = ira distribution (you) 200.00 + ira distribution (spouse) 1,000.00 + interest 28,700.00 = 29,900.00. Federal taxable income = 29,900.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 + 2 x 1,600.00 = 0.00 (floored at 0); the federal senior deduction is ignored. Form 1 line 1 federal AGI 29,900.00; line 2 Schedule I adjustments 0.00; line 3 29,900.00; line 4 additions 0.00; line 5 29,900.00. Schedule SB: line 16 retirement income subtraction: qualifying income you (age 68): IRA 200.00 = 200.00; smaller of 200.00 and the 48,000.00 cap = 200.00; line 17 $5,000 retirement income subtraction (federal AGI 29,900.00 is under 30,000.00): you smaller of 200.00 and 5,000 = 200.00; spouse smaller of 1,000.00 and 5,000 = 1,000.00 = 1,200.00; line 50 total 1,400.00. Form 1 line 6 1,400.00; line 7 Wisconsin income = 29,900.00 - 1,400.00 = 28,500.00. Line 8 standard deduction, 2025 Standard Deduction Table (Form 1 Instructions PDF page 35), row 28,500 to less than 29,000, column Married filing jointly: 25,003.00 (printed row, at least / less than / single / joint / separate / head of household: 28,500 / 29,000 / 12,456 / 25,003 / 8,892 / 15,449). Line 9 = 28,500.00 - 25,003.00 = 3,497.00. Line 10a 2 x 700 = 1,400.00; line 10b 2 x 250 = 500.00; line 10c 1,900.00. Line 11 taxable income = 3,497.00 - 1,900.00 = 1,597.00. Line 12 tax, Schedule B (joint) as numbers: 3.5% x 1,597.00 = 55.895; total 55.895, rounded once to 55.90. The Tax Table row 1,500 to 1,600 (PDF page 38) gives 54; expected keeps the schedule. Credits (lines 13-20, 30-35): none modelled; 0.00. State income tax 55.90. Form figure for comparison (line 16 200, line 17 1,000): Form 1 line 6 1,200.00; line 7 Wisconsin income = 29,900.00 - 1,200.00 = 28,700.00. Line 8 standard deduction, 2025 Standard Deduction Table (Form 1 Instructions PDF page 35), row 28,500 to less than 29,000, column Married filing jointly: 25,003.00 (printed row, at least / less than / single / joint / separate / head of household: 28,500 / 29,000 / 12,456 / 25,003 / 8,892 / 15,449). Line 9 = 28,700.00 - 25,003.00 = 3,697.00. Line 10a 2 x 700 = 1,400.00; line 10b 2 x 250 = 500.00; line 10c 1,900.00. Line 11 taxable income = 3,697.00 - 1,900.00 = 1,797.00. Line 12 tax, Schedule B (joint) as numbers: 3.5% x 1,797.00 = 62.895; total 62.895, rounded once to 62.90. The Tax Table row 1,700 to 1,800 (PDF page 38) gives 61; expected keeps the schedule. Form state income tax 62.90. The projection's tax is 7.00 lower than the form's.
accepted_approximations: The 5,000 subtraction takes only retirement income left after the 24,000/48,000 subtraction; the projection applies each to the full covered income.
The projection always takes the 24,000/48,000 subtraction for a person 67 or older, never the Wisconsin credits it bars (see not_modelled); a household whose credits are worth more would skip it.
